attacks.claim: The record cites only Family Code art. 7 para. 2 (a minor spouse may sue on the effects of the marriage) and has no slot on the plaintiff's capacity. It leaves out CPCA art. 437, the later rule written for divorce claims: when the spouse lacks full capacity, the request is filed in her name by her guardian (ولي) or curator (مقدم). It also leaves out CPCA arts. 64 and 65: lack of capacity makes the act void, and the judge raises it of his own motion.

source.what: Law 08-09 of 25 Feb 2008 (CPCA), Official Journal 2008 no. 21 (23 Apr 2008), Arabic p. 37 (art. 437) and p. 9 (arts. 64, 65); the ledger lists no later amendment of these articles (law 22-13 does not touch them)

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 437: عندما يكون الزوج ناقص الأهلية، يقدم الطلب باسمه، من قبل وليه أو مقدمه، حسب الحالة. / المادة 64: حالات بطلان العقود غير القضائية والإجراءات من حيث موضوعها محددة على سبيل الحصر فيما يأتي: 1 - انعدام الأهلية للخصوم ... / المادة 65: يثير القاضي تلقائيا انعدام الأهلية
attacks.consequence: Case: a wife married under 19 with a judge's leave, or a wife under interdiction, files the tatliq petition in her own name. The record says nothing, or implies through b48 that she may sue alone, but under CPCA 437 and 65 the petition is open to nullity raised by the court. The record should ask whether the plaintiff is under 19 or under interdiction and flag who must file. The conflict between art. 7 para. 2 (2005) and CPCA 437 (2008) should be an open point, not settled by b48 alone. The same question arises for a defendant husband under interdiction (CPCA 64 item 2: the representative's capacity).

attacks.claim: Open point o10 says no legal-aid text exists, and doc7 asks in every case for proof that court fees are paid. Ordinance 71-57, art. 28 as replaced by law 09-02, grants legal aid by operation of law to any plaintiff in a maintenance matter and to the mother in a custody matter. Those are the usual accessory requests r3 and r4 of this claim. CPCA art. 17 itself reserves cases where the law provides otherwise.

source.what: Law 09-02 of 25 Feb 2009 amending ordinance 71-57 on legal aid, art. 28 as replaced; Official Journal 2009 no. 15 (8 Mar 2009), Arabic p. 11 (French p. 10, https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2009/F2009015.pdf). Later amendments of ordinance 71-57 were not searched.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 28: تمنح المساعدة القضائية بقوة القانون إلى: ... 4 – المدعي في مادة النفقة، 5 – الأم في مادة الحضانة
attacks.consequence: When the requests include maintenance, or custody by the mother, doc7 should not present fee payment as the only way to have the petition registered. The record should point to legal aid as of right: the request goes to the legal-aid bureau with proof of the status, and the bureau decides within eight days. o10 is answered in part at tier 1 and should not stay grade D. Whether aid granted for the accessory request also covers the tatliq request itself is a reading to record.

attacks.claim: b18 and k11 present the appointment of two arbitrators as compulsory (Family Code art. 56: «وجب»). The record ignores CPCA arts. 446 to 449, the later procedural rules on the same mechanism. Art. 446 makes the appointment discretionary («جاز للقاضي»), on the condition that no harm has been proved in the proceedings. Art. 449 lets the judge end the mission of his own motion. Art. 448 makes an agreement reached by the arbitrators binding by an order open to no appeal.

source.what: Law 08-09 (CPCA), arts. 446-449, Official Journal 2008 no. 21, Arabic p. 38

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 446: إذا لم يثبت أي ضرر أثناء الخصومة، جاز للقاضي أن يعين حكمين اثنين لمحاولة الصلح بينهما حسب مقتضيات قانون الأسرة.
attacks.consequence: For the persistent-discord ground (b10) the record should show that the two texts conflict ('must' in Family Code art. 56, 'may' in CPCA 446) and not state a must as settled. It should cite CPCA 446-449 next to b18. A tier-3 lead (an academic article, univ-soukahras.dz eprint 2023-conf-8) says courts rarely appoint arbitrators. No Supreme Court decision on the point was found.

attacks.claim: Boundary n3 fires on debtor_is_foreign_national = yes alone and tells the lawyer the case is outside because foreign law applies. Its own tellingFacts, and Civil Code art. 13, require something more: neither spouse was Algerian when the marriage was made. If the wife was Algerian at the marriage, Algerian law alone governs the dissolution, whatever the husband's nationality.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 13, Official Journal 1975 no. 78, p. 991 (PDF p. 3); according to the ledger, law 05-10 did not touch it (only 13 bis and 13 bis 1 were inserted)

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 13: يسري القانون الجزائري وحده في الأحوال المنصوص عليها في المادتين 11 و12 اذا كان احد الزوجين جزائريا وقت انعقاد الزواج، الا فيما يخص اهلية الزواج
attacks.consequence: Common case: an Algerian wife married to a foreign husband. n3 warns 'outside: foreign applicable law' even though Algerian law applies by art. 13. The when-condition needs a second slot (was either spouse Algerian at the marriage?) and should fire only when both answers point abroad. The slot name 'debtor' also does not fit a tatliq defendant.

attacks.claim: For two classes of missing husbands, the record's only route is tatliq for absence (Family Code arts. 112 and 53 ground 5), and it has no boundary for them. Law 03-06 covers men missing after the 21 May 2003 earthquake. Ordinance 06-01, arts. 27-36, covers men missing in the national tragedy. Both lay down, notwithstanding the Family Code, a declaration of death by judgment on a police record of disappearance, without art. 113's four years. The judgment produces all legal effects, so the wife becomes a widow, which tatliq does not give her, and gains rights to compensation (ord. 06-01 art. 37) and legal aid as of right.

source.what: Ordinance 06-01 of 27 Feb 2006, arts. 27-37, Official Journal 2006 no. 11, Arabic p. 6 (French pp. 5-6); and Law 03-06 of 14 Jun 2003, arts. 2-3, Official Journal 2003 no. 37, Arabic p. 9 (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-ARABE/2003/A2003037.pdf; French p. 7)

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 29: بغض النظر عن الأحكام المنصوص عليها في قانون الأسرة، تطبق الأحكام الواردة في هذا القسم على المفقودين المذكورين في المادة 28 أعلاه. / المادة 36: ... وتترتب عليه مجموع الآثار القانونية المنصوص عليها في التشريع المعمول به. / (قانون 03-06) المادة 2: بغض النظر عن أحكام قانون الأسرة، تسري الأحكام الواردة أدناه على مفقودي الزلزال ...
attacks.consequence: k6 says to distinguish the missing-person regime but no item does so. Add a boundary for the wife of a husband missing in these events, pointing to the declaration of death. Caveat: both texts set short windows. Under law 03-06 the police record is issued within 8 months of the disaster. Under ord. 06-01 it is issued within one year of publication, and the court must be seized within 6 months of receiving it (art. 31). So the route may now be closed for new cases, which is why the boundary should warn and not block. Practical weight today is low. The texts were read; no amendment of them was searched.

attacks.claim: Open point o5 leaves unanswered whether abandoning the wife is an offence, and the criminal-proceedings slot is attached only to the harm element e4. Penal Code art. 330 (2), as replaced by law 15-19, makes it an offence for a husband to leave his wife wilfully for more than two months without serious cause. So the desertion and absence grounds (e2) also routinely overlap a criminal case. Arts. 266 bis and 266 bis 1, added by the same law, make violence against a spouse an offence; under those articles the victim's pardon ends prosecution and conjugal violence may be proved by any means.

source.what: Law 15-19 of 30 Dec 2015 amending the Penal Code, arts. 2-4 (new arts. 266 bis, 266 bis 1, 330, 330 bis), Official Journal 2015 no. 71, Arabic p. 4 (French pp. 3-4). Penal Code amendments after 2015 were not searched.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 330: يعاقب بالحبس من ستة (6) أشهر إلى سنتين (2) وبغرامة من 50.000 دج إلى 200.000 دج: ... 2 – الزوج الذي يتخلى عمدا ولمدة تتجاوز شهرين (2) عن زوجته وذلك لغير سبب جدي.
attacks.consequence: Attach criminal_case_on_same_facts (and the x6 exit) to e2 as well as e4. Answer o5 in part at tier 1: abandonment of the wife for over two months and spousal violence are offences. Add the 330 (2) complaint or judgment to doc4 as a possible proof of desertion or absence.

attacks.claim: t1 sends tatliq only to the court of the marital home (CPCA arts. 40 para. 3 and 426). A common case has no answer: the couple's last marital home was abroad (Algerian emigrants), and the wife returns to Algeria and files there. No Algerian court has the marital home in its area. The record's only nuance, o8, covers a wife who has left the home, not a home outside Algeria.

source.what: Law 08-09 (CPCA), art. 426 item 3, Official Journal 2008 no. 21, Arabic p. 36; art. 37 (general rule: the defendant's domicile, unless the law provides otherwise) and art. 47 (territorial objection raised before any defence), same issue

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 426: تكون المحكمة مختصة إقليميا: ... 3 - في موضوع الطلاق أو الرجوع بمكان وجود المسكن الزوجي
attacks.consequence: The record would propose 'court of the marital home' and leave the lawyer with no court, or with a guess. It should ask whether the marital home was in Algeria. If it was not, it should warn that no text names the court, and record the candidate readings as an open point: the defendant's domicile or last domicile under art. 37, or the plaintiff's domicile. No Supreme Court decision on the point was found in this search.

attacks.claim: The documents list does not mention CPCA art. 8 para. 2. Documents must be in Arabic or come with an official translation, on pain of inadmissibility. In this claim that often bites: marriage certificates drawn up abroad, foreign medical certificates, foreign judgments (k29 and k55 foresee the foreign element).

source.what: Law 08-09 (CPCA), art. 8, Official Journal 2008 no. 21, Arabic p. 4

attacks.quoteArabic: يجب أن تقدم الوثائق والمستندات باللغة العربية أو مصحوبة بترجمة رسمية إلى هذه اللغة، تحت طائلة عدم القبول.
attacks.consequence: doc1 and doc4 should carry the condition 'in Arabic or with an official translation'. Where the marriage was made abroad, the lawyer should be told to check its transcription in the Algerian civil-status registers before relying on the extract (b19).
